intro: “A / an” means one thing that is not specific; “the” means a specific thing. But English often uses no article at all: “I like coffee”, not “I like the coffee”. This lesson explains when to use a, an, the… or nothing.
objectifs: Choose between a and an by the sound (not the letter) that follows.
Use “a / an” for a thing that is not specific, a job or a first mention.
Use “the” for a specific thing, a thing you already know about, or a unique thing.
Know when to use no article: general ideas, meals, languages, sports, most countries, at home, by bus.

sections.titre: A or an? The sound decides
texte: “A” and “an” have the same meaning. Use “an” before a word that starts with a vowel SOUND, and “a” before a consonant sound. The pronunciation is important, not the spelling.

So “hour” starts with a silent h (a vowel sound) → an hour. “University” starts with the sound /j/ (like “you”) → a university. For abbreviations, listen to the name of the first letter: an MBA (/em/), a UFO (/juː/).

lignes: a book, a car, a house, a big apple
u and eu sounding /juː/; o sounding /w/
a university, a European city, a one-way ticket
an apple, an egg, an idea, an old man, an umbrella
an hour, an honest person, an heir
an abbreviation starting with a vowel sound
an MP, an X-ray, an FBI agent

sections.note: Only the word right after the article matters: an apple but a red apple; a house but an old house.

texte: Use “a / an” only before a singular countable noun. It has no plural: in the plural, use nothing or “some” (lesson 31): a book → books / some books.

Uses: one thing or person among others, not specific; the first time you talk about it; a job or a type of person (necessary in English); the meaning “one”; frequency and price (twice a week, 3 euros a kilo); exclamations (What a beautiful day!).
exemples: A job: the article is necessary.
We go to the gym three times a week.

texte: “The” is the same for singular and plural, countable and uncountable nouns. It shows that we know which thing we mean.

Uses: something you mentioned before (first a, then the); something the rest of the sentence makes clear (the man in the blue shirt); something clear in the situation (Close the door, the kitchen); something unique (the sun, the moon, the world, the internet); some places and media (the cinema, the theatre, the radio); musical instruments (play the piano); family names in the plural (the Martins); seas, rivers and oceans (the Atlantic, the Seine); and countries with a plural or long name (the UK, the USA, the Netherlands).
exemples: I've got a cat and a dog. The cat is black.
The woman in the red coat is my aunt.
The sun is very hot today.

texte: To talk about something in general, English uses NO article with plural and uncountable nouns: I like cats (cats in general), Coffee is expensive, Life is beautiful. If you say “the cats”, you mean specific cats.

Also no article before: meals (have breakfast, at lunch), languages and school subjects (English is easy, I study history), sports (play football), most countries, cities and continents (France, Paris, Africa), days, months and holidays (on Monday, in June, at Christmas), and in fixed expressions: at home, at work, at school, in bed, go to school, go to bed, by bus, by car.

lignes: I have the lunch at noon.
She's at the home / at the work.
I go to the work by the bus.
I go to work by bus.

sections.note: Compare: “I like music” (music in general) / “I like the music in this film” (the specific music of this film).

texte: To choose, ask two questions. 1) Is it specific, known to both people, or unique? → the. 2) If not, is it a singular countable noun? → a / an. If not (plural or uncountable, in general) → no article.
“The” sounds like /ðə/ before a consonant sound (the book) and often /ði/ before a vowel sound (the apple), but many speakers today say /ðə/ everywhere.
exemples: There's a bank near here. The bank opens at nine.
Dogs are friendly, but the dog next door is noisy.

formule: a + consonant sound · an + vowel sound · the = specific / known / unique · Ø = general idea (plural, uncountable), meals, languages, sports, at home, by bus
prononciation: “a” is almost always weak: /ə/ (a book /ə bʊk/). The strong form /eɪ/ is only for emphasis.
“an” joins the next word: an apple /ə ˈnæpl/, an hour /ə ˈnaʊə/.
“the”: /ðə/ before a consonant sound (the car), /ði/ before a vowel sound (the end). Strong form /ðiː/ for emphasis: “THE best”.
The /ð/ sound in “the”: tongue between the teeth, voice on. Don't say “ze” or “de”.
Don't drop the small /ə/ of “a”: “She's a nurse” has three syllables: /ʃiːz ə ˈnɜːs/.
erreurs: General idea in the plural: no article.
A job in the singular: a / an is necessary.
No article before a sport; but play the piano (instrument).

dialogue.contexte: Two friends look for a restaurant in the evening in Brussels.
lignes: I'm hungry. Is there a good restaurant near here?
Yes, there's an Italian restaurant and a Cameroonian restaurant on the next street.
an before the vowel sound of Italian.
I love Cameroonian food! Is the Cameroonian restaurant expensive?
food in general: no article; then the (second mention).
No, it isn't. And the owner is very friendly. She's a chef from Douala.
Great. What time does it close?
At eleven. We've got an hour and a half.
Perfect. I usually have dinner at home, so this is a nice change!
Let's go by tram. The stop is just there.
by tram: no article; the stop: clear in the situation.

mots: a thing that protects you from rain
The film is two hours long.
She studies at a university in Ghent.
The owner of the shop is my uncle.
the star that gives us light and heat
It's the biggest city in the world.
the Earth and all its countries
the first meal of the day
What do you eat for lunch?
the meal in the middle of the day
the main meal in the evening
a big musical instrument with black and white keys

exercices.consigne: Complete with a, an, the or Ø (no article).
items: I've got a sister and a brother. ___ sister lives in Lille.
We go to work by ___ bus.
(Music / The music) in this café is too loud.
(English / The English) is an international language.
(Water / The water) in this bottle is cold.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Correct it.
items: I have the lunch at one o'clock.
I have lunch at one o'clock.
We study at an university in Liège.
We study at a university in Liège.

exercices.consigne: Complete each sentence with a, an, the or Ø, and write the whole sentence.
items: I like sport and music. (US: sports)
She goes to ___ school by ___ bike.
She goes to school by bike.

exercices.consigne: Write four sentences about you: your job (a / an), something you like in general (no article), something specific in your home (the), and a habit with a fixed expression (at home, by bus…).
items: I'm an accountant. I love books and good coffee. The kitchen in my flat is very small. I usually go to work by train, and I have dinner at home.

a_retenir: a + consonant sound, an + vowel sound: a university, an hour.
a / an: one of many, first mention, job (She's a nurse), frequency (twice a week).
the: already known, made specific, unique, instruments (play the piano).
No article for general ideas: I like cats, Life is short, Coffee is good.
No article: meals, languages, sports, at home, at work, go to bed, by bus.
